clue.text: Split, or stick together, being caught with time off

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
leave is time away from work

explanation.surface: Someone splits from a partner or stays loyal after being caught taking unauthorised time off.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is itself a pair of opposites: to cleave can mean to cut apart or to cling to.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb has two opposite senses: to chop apart with a blade, and to adhere closely, as in a contronym.

clue.text: In Mali, a natural climber

indicators.note: In says the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: In the West African country there is a born climber.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters span three words: maLI A NAtural; the whole clue also describes a tropical vine.
explanation.definitionFit: A liana is a woody climbing vine of tropical forests, a plant that climbs by nature.

clue.text: Sent up a Roman Catholic to state capital

indicators.note: sent up in a down clue means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: CA is the postal abbreviation of California, a US state

explanation.surface: A Catholic is dispatched to a state capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state capital' is one phrase in the surface, but state gives CA and only 'capital' defines Accra, capital of Ghana.
explanation.definitionFit: Accra is the capital city of Ghana in West Africa.

clue.text: Teaches nonsense if ideas only partly recalled

indicators.note: recalled says the hidden letters are read backwards
only partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An instructor talks rubbish when remembering concepts only half-way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns SEIFIDE, found in nonsenSE IF IDEas, backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To edify is to instruct or improve someone morally or intellectually, so teaches is a synonym.

clue.text: Radar perhaps surprisingly protected after power cut

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests the letters turn up in an unexpected arrangement
cut means the letter for power is removed from the word before it

parts.note: P is the standard abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: A radar station is unexpectedly well guarded following a blackout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' removes P (power) from PROTECTED, leaving ROTECTED, which 'surprisingly' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Radar is one kind of instrument for sensing objects, so it is an example of the wider class.

clue.text: Stupidly refuse to accept bottomless ego

indicators.note: to accept means the word for refuse takes the other piece inside it

parts.note: to deny is to refuse

indicators.note: bottomless in a down clue drops the last letter

parts.note: the self is one's ego

explanation.surface: Someone foolishly declines to accept an endless ego.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottomless' works in a down clue, where the last letter is the bottom; 'to accept' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Dense means dim-witted, so densely means in a dull, stupid way.

clue.text: Suggest, or reject, flip of coin elsewhere

parts.note: a toss is a flip of a coin
out means away or elsewhere, as in 'she's out'

explanation.surface: Someone proposes or rejects a coin toss being held somewhere else.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is two opposites: to toss out an idea is to propose it; to toss out a thing is to discard it.
explanation.definitionFit: To toss out can mean to float an idea casually, or to throw something away.

clue.text: One of the limits of canteen: very small plate for breakfast cereal

parts.words: One of the limits of canteen
parts.note: the limits of canteen are C and N, and one of them is spelt out literally as 'C or N'
a flake is a thin small plate or layer

explanation.surface: A tiny plate at the canteen, meant for breakfast cereal.
explanation.walkthrough: The ends of 'canteen' are C and N; 'One of' them is read literally as C OR N, giving CORN.
explanation.definitionFit: A cornflake is one flake of a well-known toasted maize breakfast food.

clue.text: Supervision (or neglect) of deliveries, given stated location

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries, so it stands for deliveries

indicators.note: stated means the word for location is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a site is a location

explanation.surface: A manager supervises, or overlooks, parcel deliveries depending on the address.
explanation.walkthrough: Overs are cricket's units of six balls. The definition is two opposites: oversight is watchful supervision, and also a failure to notice.
explanation.definitionFit: Oversight means management or watching over, yet also an error from not noticing something.

clue.text: Permit, or penalise, criminal actions? Not at first

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters are bent out of their lawful order
at first takes only the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A question of whether misdeeds should be allowed or punished, the first instinct being to say no.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges ACTIONS to SANCTIO, then N (first letter of 'Not'). The definition is a pair of opposites: sanction can approve or punish.
explanation.definitionFit: A sanction is both an official authorisation and a penalty imposed on a state or person.

clue.text: Hide, or show, Native American between two poles

indicators.note: between places one piece inside the pair of letters given by the poles

parts.note: S and N are the south and north poles
the Cree are a Native American people

explanation.surface: A tepee, hidden or displayed, with a Native American standing between two tent poles.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is two opposites: a screen conceals things, and also displays a film or picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To screen is to shield from view, yet also to project a film for an audience.

clue.text: Rifle protecting a revolutionary, or an officer

indicators.note: protecting means the gun wraps around the next piece

parts.note: a carbine is a short rifle

indicators.note: revolutionary means the following short word is turned round

explanation.surface: A firearm guarding either a rebel or a policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' looks like a noun for a rebel but turns 'or' backwards to RO.
explanation.definitionFit: A carabinero is a member of the Spanish or Latin American armed police, an officer in that force.

clue.text: Moving rapidly, or stuck when grabbed by foot

indicators.note: grabbed by means the word for when is held inside the abbreviation

parts.note: FT is the abbreviation for foot as a unit of length
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Something runs quickly, or gets stuck once someone seizes it by the foot.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a pair of opposites: fast means speedy, and also firmly fixed, as in 'stuck fast'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fast describes great speed, but also something held immovably, as in a boat made fast.

clue.text: Sides with, or switches before saying "cheerio"

parts.note: switches are thin sticks or canes

indicators.note: saying signals the word for cheerio is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: cheerio is a British way to say goodbye, or bye

explanation.surface: Someone backs a friend, or changes allegiance, before saying goodbye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or switches' looks like part of a two-way definition, but switches gives STICKS; 'saying' turns BYE into BY.
explanation.definitionFit: To stick by someone is to stay loyal and take their side.

clue.text: Parisian can work before I briefly return

parts.note: toil means work

indicators.note: return means the shortened word is read backwards
briefly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: I, in a crossword, is the setter of the puzzle

explanation.surface: A French tin is used for work before the speaker comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' is the setter, shortened by 'briefly' to SETTE and turned by 'return' to ETTES.
explanation.definitionFit: Toilettes is French for toilets, and can is slang for a lavatory, so it is what a Parisian calls one.

clue.text: Against hollow man and Tory cavorting? That's self-contradictory

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons

indicators.note: cavorting suggests the letters leap about into a new order
hollow means the word is emptied, leaving only its outside letters

explanation.surface: An empty-headed man opposes a Conservative's antics, which seems inconsistent.
explanation.walkthrough: MN (the hollow 'man') and TORY are rearranged by 'cavorting' into TRONYM. The answer names this puzzle's theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A contronym is a word with two opposite meanings, such as cleave, so it contradicts itself.

clue.text: Wasn't mad about type of string sounds from banjo, maybe

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the next piece
mad suggests the letters of the contraction go wild

parts.note: a G-string is a type of string garment, or the G string of an instrument

explanation.surface: Someone was not keen on a particular string on their banjo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mad' rearranges WASNT into TWANS, and 'about' puts G inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A twang is the resonant note of a plucked string, typical of a banjo, hence 'maybe'.

clue.text: After a short time, gained back unimpressive catch

parts.note: MIN is short for minute, a short time

indicators.note: back means the word for gained is read from right to left

parts.note: won means gained

explanation.surface: An angler, after a while, got back what turned out to be a small catch.
explanation.definitionFit: A minnow is a tiny freshwater fish, so a disappointing haul for an angler; figuratively an insignificant person.

clue.text: Become worn down, or endure topic of desultory conversation

definitions.meaning: both to erode and to survive a storm, two opposite senses
the classic subject of idle small talk

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is itself a pair of opposites: weather can mean erode or withstand.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock weathers by eroding, a company weathers a crisis by surviving, and the British talk about it endlessly.

clue.text: Member wearing man's clothes

indicators.note: wearing means the outer word has the other piece on it, like a garment around it

parts.note: the Gents is a British name for a men's lavatory, read as man's
an arm is a limb, or member, of the body

explanation.surface: A club member is dressed in men's clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The Gents is the usual British name for a men's public toilet, so 'man's' stands for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Garments are items of clothing, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Add or take away new gaudy covering

indicators.note: covering means the word for gaudy goes around the letter

parts.note: garish means gaudy

explanation.surface: Someone adds or removes a fresh, flashy cover.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is two opposites: garnish means decorate food, and also seize wages by legal order.
explanation.definitionFit: Garnishing a dish adds trimmings, while garnishing earnings takes money away under a court order.

clue.text: Nuclear device's designer about to be demoted

indicators.note: demoted means the letter is moved further down the word, in a down clue

parts.note: a creator is a designer or maker
C is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: The engineer behind an atomic device is about to lose rank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' looks like a phrase meaning 'soon', but about gives C, and 'to be demoted' moves it down inside CREATOR. The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A reactor is the apparatus in which a nuclear chain reaction is controlled.

clue.text: Look for someone at one's own level, or higher?

definitions.meaning: a ... is an equal, as in '... group'
a noble, someone of higher rank

explanation.surface: Seeking out a social equal, or someone above you.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions; the last two are opposites, an equal or a superior, making peer a self-contradicting word.
explanation.definitionFit: Peer means to gaze, an equal, and a member of the nobility, such as a lord.

clue.text: Skill of crew aboard the Hindenburg?

definitions.text: Skill of crew aboard the Hindenburg?

indicators.note: aboard means one piece goes inside the vessel

parts.note: the Hindenburg was a famous German airship
to man a vessel is to crew it

explanation.surface: The flying ability of the men operating the Hindenburg.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hindenburg was the German airship destroyed in 1937; 'crew' is a verb here, and the whole clue also defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Airmanship is skill in flying aircraft, exactly what a crew aloft would need.

clue.text: Removes or supplies kernels

definitions.meaning: to seed fruit is to take out its pips
to seed a field is to sow it with grains

explanation.walkthrough: The two definitions share 'kernels'; seed is a word with opposite meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeding grapes removes their pips, while seeding a lawn puts grain into the soil.

clue.text: Seeing all but not the top of the cake

indicators.note: all but means everything except the word that follows is kept

parts.note: noticing means seeing

explanation.surface: Someone sees everything except the top of the cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all but not' reads as one phrase, but 'all but' says the word 'not' is taken away from NOTICING.
explanation.definitionFit: Icing is the sugary coating spread on top of a cake.

clue.text: Husband follows peculiar scent or horrible smell

indicators.note: follows places the letter after the rearranged word
peculiar suggests the letters are strangely arranged

explanation.surface: A husband trails an odd perfume, or perhaps a dreadful whiff.
explanation.definitionFit: A stench is a strong, foul odour, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Bold, or at first lost in terrible perdition

indicators.note: terrible suggests the remaining letters are thrown into disorder
lost in means that letter goes missing from the word that follows
at first takes only the opening letter of the short word

explanation.surface: Someone is daring, or else ruined in dreadful damnation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' looks like it offers a second definition, as elsewhere in this puzzle, but its first letter O is removed from PERDITION, and 'terrible' rearranges PERDITIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Intrepid means fearless, a synonym for bold.

clue.text: It has the same shape as Moorish palace's first construction

definitions.text: It has the same shape as

indicators.note: construction means the letters are built up into a new arrangement
first takes only the opening letter of the word for palace

explanation.surface: A building is said to mirror a Moorish palace's original form.
explanation.walkthrough: P (first of 'palace's') joins MOORISH, and 'construction' rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: An isomorph is a thing, such as a crystal, of identical form or structure to another.

clue.text: Leave (or again join) regime restricting society

indicators.note: restricting means the word for regime holds the next letter within it

parts.note: a reign is a period of rule, a regime

explanation.surface: A member quits, or rejoins, an organisation whose rules curb society.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is two opposites: resign means quit, and re-sign means sign up again.
explanation.definitionFit: To resign is to give up a post; read as re-sign it means to sign on a second time.
